If $b$ is very small as compared to the value of $a$, so that the cube and other higher powers of $\dfrac{b}{a}$ can be neglected in the identity

questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{1}{a - b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 2b} + \dfrac{1}{a - 3b} + \ldots . + \dfrac{1}{a - nb}$

$= {\left(a - b\right)}^{- 1} + {\left(a - 2b\right)}^{- 1} + \ldots . + {\left(a - nb\right)}^{- 1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{a}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}{\left(1 - \dfrac{rb}{a}\right)}^{- 1}$

So $\gamma = \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{3{a}^{3}}$

${a}_{r} = cos\dfrac{2r\pi}{9} + isin\dfrac{2r\pi}{9}, r = 1, 2, 3, \ldots , i = \sqrt{- 1}$

From Euler form ${e}^{i\theta} = cos\theta + isin\theta$

$\left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ {a}_{4} & {a}_{5} & {a}_{6} \\ {a}_{7} & {a}_{8} & {a}_{9}\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left|\begin{cases}{e}^{i\dfrac{2\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{4\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{6\pi}{9}} \\ {e}^{i\dfrac{8\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{i10\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{12\pi}{9}} \\ {e}^{i\dfrac{14\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{i16\pi}{9}} & {e}^{i\dfrac{18\pi}{9}}\end{cases}\right|$

$= 0 - - - ( II )$

From equation $( II ) \text{ and } ( III )$

$\left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ {a}_{4} & {a}_{5} & {a}_{6} \\ {a}_{7} & {a}_{8} & {a}_{9}\end{cases}\right| = {a}_{1}{a}_{9} - {a}_{3}{a}_{7}$

questions.q:
If $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\pi,$ then the system of equations

$x + \left(cos\gamma\right)y + \left(cos\beta\right)z = 0$

$\left(cos\gamma\right)x + y + \left(cos\alpha\right)z = 0$

$\left(cos\beta\right)x + \left(cos\alpha\right)y + z = 0$

has :
questions.solution:
Given, $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 2\pi$

Now, $\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}1 & cos\gamma & cos\beta \\ cos\gamma & 1 & cos\alpha \\ cos\beta & cos\alpha & 1\end{cases}\right|$

By expanding along the first column, we get

$∆ = 1\left(1 - \cos^{2}\alpha\right) - cos\gamma\left(cos\gamma - cos\alpha . cos\beta\right) + cos\beta\left(cos\alpha . cos\gamma - cos\beta\right)$

$∆ = 1 - \cos^{2}\alpha - \cos^{2}\gamma + cos\gamma . cos\alpha . cos\beta + cos\beta . cos\alpha . cos\gamma - \cos^{2}\beta$

$= 1 - \cos^{2}\alpha - \cos^{2}\beta - \cos^{2}\gamma + 2cos\alpha . cos\beta . cos\gamma$

$= \sin^{2}\alpha - \cos^{2}\beta - cos\gamma ( cos\gamma - 2cos\alpha . cos\beta )$

$= - cos ( \alpha + \beta ) . cos ( \alpha - \beta ) - cos\gamma\left[cos\left\{2\pi - ( \alpha + \beta )\right\} - 2cos\alpha . cos\beta\right]$

$= - cos ( 2\pi - \gamma ) cos ( \alpha - \beta ) - cos\gamma\left[cos ( \alpha + \beta ) - 2cos\alpha . cos\beta\right]$

$= - cos ( 2\pi - \gamma ) . cos ( \alpha - \beta ) - cos\gamma\left[cos\alpha . cos\beta - sin\alpha . sin\beta - 2cos\alpha . cos\beta\right]$

$= - cos\gamma . cos ( \alpha - \beta ) + cos\gamma . cos ( \alpha - \beta )$

$= 0$

So, $∆ = 0$

Hence, the system of equations has infinitely many solutions.

questions.solution:
Given,

$S$ be the set of all values of $\theta \in [ - \pi, \pi ]$ for which the system of linear equations
$x + y + \sqrt{3}z = 0$
$- x + ( tan\theta ) y + \sqrt{7}z = 0$
$x + y + ( tan\theta ) z = 0$
has non-trivial solution,

So, by condition of non-trivial solution we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & \sqrt{3} \\ - 1 & tan\theta & \sqrt{7} \\ 1 & 1 & tan\theta\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(\tan^{2}\theta - \sqrt{7}\right) - \left(- tan\theta - \sqrt{7}\right) + \sqrt{3}\left(- 1 - tan\theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta + \left(1 - \sqrt{3}\right)tan\theta - \sqrt{3} = 0$

$⇒ \left(tan\theta + 1\right)\left(tan\theta - \sqrt{3}\right) = 0$

$⇒ tan\theta = \sqrt{3}, - 1$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{- 2\pi}{3}, \dfrac{- \pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Hence,

$\dfrac{120}{\pi} ∑ \theta = 120\left(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}\right) = 20$

Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $14{x}^{2} - 31x + 3\lambda = 0$ and $\alpha, \gamma$ be the roots of the equation $35{x}^{2} - 53x + 4\lambda = 0$. Then $\dfrac{3\alpha}{\beta}$ and $\dfrac{4\alpha}{\gamma}$ are the roots of the equation :
questions.solution:
Given $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the below equation

$14{x}^{2} - 31x + 3\lambda = 0$

So, $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{31}{14} \ldots \left(1\right)$

And, $\alpha\beta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{14} \ldots \left(2\right)$

Given $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ are roots of the below equation

$35{x}^{2} - 53x + 4\lambda = 0$

So, $\alpha + \gamma = \dfrac{53}{35} \ldots \left(3\right)$

And, $\alpha\gamma = \dfrac{4\lambda}{35} \ldots \left(4\right)$

On dividing equation$\left(2\right)$ and equation $\left(4\right)$,

$\dfrac{\beta}{\gamma} = \dfrac{3 \times 35}{4 \times 14} = \dfrac{15}{8} ⇒ \beta = \dfrac{15}{8}\gamma$

On subtracting equation $\left(1\right)$ and equation $\left(3\right)$,

$⇒ \beta - \gamma = \dfrac{31}{14} - \dfrac{53}{35} = \dfrac{155 - 106}{70} = \dfrac{7}{10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{15}{8}\gamma - \gamma = \dfrac{7}{10} ⇒ \gamma = \dfrac{4}{5}$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{15}{8} \times \dfrac{4}{5} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

So, $\alpha = \dfrac{31}{14} - \beta = \dfrac{31}{14} - \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

And $\lambda = \dfrac{14}{3}\alpha\beta = \dfrac{14}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{7} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 5$

So, the sum of the roots of the required equation,

$\dfrac{3\alpha}{\beta} + \dfrac{4\alpha}{\gamma} = \left(\dfrac{3\alpha\gamma + 4\alpha\beta}{\beta\gamma}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\left(3 \times \dfrac{4\lambda}{35} + 4 \times \dfrac{3\lambda}{14}\right)}{\beta\gamma} = \dfrac{12\lambda\left(14 + 35\right)}{14 \times 35\beta\gamma}$

$= \dfrac{49 \times 12 \times 5}{490 \times \dfrac{3}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{5}} = 5$

And the product of the roots of the required equation,

So, the required equation is

${x}^{2} - ( \text{sum of roots} ) x + \text{product of roots} = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} - 5x + \dfrac{250}{49} = 0$

$⇒ 49{x}^{2} - 245x + 250 = 0$

Now let ${e}^{x} = t$ we get,

${t}^{4} + 8{t}^{3} + 13{t}^{2} - 8t + 1 = 0$

Now divide complete equation by ${t}^{2}$

$⇒ {t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}} + 8\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + 13 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)}^{2} + 8\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + 15 = 0$

Now let $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = z$ we get,

$⇒ {z}^{2} + 8z + 15 = 0$

$⇒ z = - 3, - 5$

So, $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = - 3$ or $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = - 5$

$⇒ {t}^{2} + 3t - 1 = 0$ or ${t}^{2} + 5t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{- 3 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}, \dfrac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{2}$

So, $x = ln\left(\alpha\right), ln\left(\beta\right)$ are both negative,

Hence, there are two solution and both are negative.

questions.q: Let ${x}_{i}\left(1 \le i \le 10\right)$ be ten observation of a random variable $X$. If $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - p\right) = 3$ and $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}{\left({x}_{i} - p\right)}^{2} = 9$ where $0 \ne p \in R$, then the standard deviation of these observations is:
questions.solution:
Standard Deviation $\left(S . D .\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}{\left({x}_{i} - p\right)}^{2}}{10} - {\left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - p\right)}{10}\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{10} - {\left(\dfrac{3}{10}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{9}{10}$

$32 + 8\alpha + 9\beta = \left(8 + \alpha + \beta\right) \times 6$

$⇒ 2\alpha + 3\beta = 16 . . . \left(1\right)$

Also, for the variance, ${\sigma}^{2} = \mathop{∑ {f}_{i}{\left({x}_{i} - x\right)}^{2}}_{i = 1}^{4}\mathop{∑ {f}_{i}}_{i = 1}^{4}$

$64 + 4\alpha + 9\beta = \left(8 + \alpha + \beta\right) \times 6 . 8$

$⇒ 640 + 40\alpha + 90\beta = 544 + 68\alpha + 68\beta$

$⇒ 28\alpha - 22\beta = 96$

$⇒ 14\alpha - 11\beta = 48 . . . \left(2\right)$

from $\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$

$\alpha = 5 \text{ and } \beta = 2$

so, new mean $= \dfrac{32 + 35 + 18}{15} = \dfrac{85}{15} = \dfrac{17}{3}$

questions.q: The first of the two samples in a group has $100$ items with mean $15$ and standard deviation $3 .$ If the whole group has $250$ items with mean $15 . 6$ and standard deviation $\sqrt{13 . 44},$ then the standard deviation of the second sample is:
questions.solution:
We have, number of terms in the first group ${n}_{1} = 100$ with their mean ${X}_{1} = 15$ and number of terms in whole group is ${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} = 250$ and their mean $X = 15 . 6 .$

Variance of first group${V}_{1}\left(x\right) = 9$ and whole group is $Var \left(x\right) = 13 . 44 .$

Now, ${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{\sigma}_{1}^{2} + {n}_{2}{\sigma}_{2}^{2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}} + \dfrac{{n}_{1}{n}_{2}}{{\left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)}^{2}}{\left(\overset{¯}{x}1 - \overset{¯}{x}2\right)}^{2}$

and ${n}_{2} = 150, \overset{¯}{x}2 = 16, {V}_{2} ( x ) = {\sigma}_{2}$

Therefore, $13 . 44 = \dfrac{100 \times 9 + 150 \times {\sigma}_{2}^{2}}{250} + \dfrac{100 \times 150}{{\left(250\right)}^{2}} \times 1$

$⇒ {\sigma}_{2}^{2} = 16$

$⇒ {\sigma}_{2} = 4$

questions.q:
Let $\mu$ be the mean and $\sigma$ be the standard deviation of the distribution

${X}_{i}$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$
${f}_{i}$ $k + 2$ $2k$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} + 1$ $k - 3$

where $Σ{f}_{i} = 62$. If $\left[x\right]$ denotes the greatest integer $\le x$, then$\left[{\mu}^{2} + {\sigma}^{2}\right]$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given,

${X}_{i}$ $0$ $1$ $2$ $3$ $4$ $5$
${f}_{i}$ $k + 2$ $2k$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} - 1$ ${k}^{2} + 1$ $k - 3$

Now we know that,

$\text{Mean} = \dfrac{∑ {X}_{i}{f}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}}$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{2k + 2{k}^{2} – 2 + 3{k}^{2} – 3 + 4{k}^{2} + 4 + 5k – 15}{62}$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{9{k}^{2} + 7k - 16}{62} . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

And $∑ {f}_{i} = 62$

$⇒ 3{k}^{2} + 4k - 2 = 62$

$⇒ 3{k}^{2} + 4k - 64 = 0$

$⇒ ( 3k + 16 ) ( k - 4 ) = 0$

$⇒ k = 4$

Now putting the value of $k$ in above equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\mu = \dfrac{156}{62}$

Now finding variance we get,

${\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {\left({X}_{i}\right)}^{2}{f}_{i}}{∑ {f}_{i}} - {\left(\text{Mean}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{1 \cdot \left(2k\right) + 4\left({k}^{2} - 1\right) + 9\left({k}^{2} - 1\right) + 16\left({k}^{2} + 1\right) + 25\left(k - 3\right)}{62} - {\left(\dfrac{156}{62}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{29{k}^{2} + 27k - 72}{62} - {\mu}^{2}$

Now putting the value of $k$ in above equation we get,

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} = \dfrac{500}{62} - {\mu}^{2}$

$⇒ {\sigma}^{2} + {\mu}^{2} = \dfrac{500}{62}$

$⇒ \left[{\sigma}^{2} + {\mu}^{2}\right] = 8$
